field: numerics (linear algebra: almost block diagonal systems, PLU factorization, determinant)

claim.location: Shipped test program at the end of the source file 546.gz (the program's own reference constant): DATA sets an 11th-order almost block diagonal system (NBLOKS = 5, N = 11). The program calls SLVBLK, then DTBLOK for the determinant, prints DET, and checks ERROR = DET - 2.418821899E6.

reference.file: the Fortran source file 546 (inside 546.gz), the test program constant 2.418821899E6 and its check ERROR = DET - 2.418821899E6
reference.sha256: not computed for the member; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.paper_value: Value 2.418821899E6 in the shipped test program, as the determinant of the fixed 11 by 11 test matrix. The paper's text is not read; the claim is the code's own reference constant.
claim.metric: DET = DETSGN * EXP(DETLOG) computed by DTBLOK for the shipped test matrix, compared as an absolute number with 2.418821899E6
claim.determinism: deterministic (fixed DATA test matrix; no random numbers)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The code is single precision (REAL), and DTBLOK forms the determinant from a sum of logarithms followed by EXP. Each single-precision operation contributes about 6e-8 relative error; for a few dozen operations the expected drift is at most about 2e-6 relative, which is about 5 on 2.4e6. The printed DET has 9 significant digits, so print rounding is negligible. A wrong pivot order, a wrong block sign or a wrong block size changes the determinant by far more than 5. Not to be loosened after any run.
